blockingIssues.problem: The idea's rationale asserts that the added "Preserve Editorial Intent" rule caused the shift toward orchestration in the candidate runs. The source documents a controlled comparison where only the Narrative.user.prompt was changed and reports an association between that change and the observed output shift, but it does not establish definitive causation. The experiment report also records limitations that undermine a causal claim (possible model backend changes, no seed/temperature control, small sample), and it notes other possible contributing factors (an internal tension in the baseline Synthesis).
blockingIssues.sourceEvidence: Prompt change: candidate added one generic section, “Preserve Editorial Intent from the Synthesis.” Controlled comparison/configuration: “Candidate: Three new runs with only src/Nueyon.Compose.Application/Prompts/Narrative/Narrative.user.prompt.txt changed. All other prompt files and workflow inputs remained identical.” Results/analysis: “Candidate outputs were readable and coherent, but consistently subordinated company identity and audience scope while making orchestration the central positioning.” Decision/analysis: “Candidate was worse on mean score... failed the orchestration hierarchy and factual restraint gates... introduced regressions.” Limitations: “the model provider may change the backend behind an alias.” “No seed or temperature override was available. Three runs per condition show consistency in these samples, not statistical significance.” “The baseline Synthesis pairs company identity with Compose... That internal tension may have reinforced the technical angle.”
blockingIssues.constraint: The source supports an observed association between the prompt change and output shift but does not support a definitive causal claim that the added rule was the cause.
